signals.title: @BashaReport: Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council affirmed that the state is moving decisively toward restoring its institutions, reasserting full sov
signals.content: Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council affirmed that the state is moving decisively toward restoring its institutions, reasserting full sovereign authority over every part of Yemen, and bringing an end to the humanitarian suffering caused by the Iran-backed Houthis. Meeting today under the chairmanship of @PresidentRashad, Chairman of the Presidential Leadership Council, and with the participation of all Council members, @sultan_alaradah, @tarikyemen, @AbuZar3a, @ALalimiBawzer, @OthmanMujalli, @malsubihi1, and @alkhnbshys3, the Council declared that the armed forces and all military formations are at a high state of combat readiness and fully prepared to carry out their constitutional duties. The Council stressed that the armed forces are prepared to seize and maintain the initiative, confront Houthi escalation with force, and impose a far heavier price on the militia's leadership, military capabilities, command structure, and sources of financing. The meeting, attended by Prime Minister @Shaya_Zindani, focused on military, security, and economic developments and the state's strategic options for confronting the Houthis' continuing escalation. The Council stressed that restoring state institutions and ending the coup remain central national objectives. The Council reviewed detailed military and security briefings on battlefield developments, combat readiness across the fronts, and continuing threats and attacks against vital infrastructure and civilian facilities. It also discussed the state's strategy for the next phase, including urgent economic and security measures to strengthen the home front, improve living conditions, and intensify the fight against terrorism, smuggling, and organized crime. The Council directed the armed forces and security agencies to take all lawful and necessary measures to defend citizens, sovereign facilities, and national interests. It stressed the importance of proactive operations against sources of hostile threats, command-and-control centers, and military capabilities being used or prepared for attacks against the armed forces, civilians, and vital infrastructure. The Presidential Leadership Council praised the combat effectiveness demonstrated by the armed forces and security services in confronting the latest wave of Houthi escalation. It commended their success in breaking militia attacks, inflicting heavy losses on hostile capabilities, and striking high-value military targets. The Council said these operations demonstrate a significant shift in the state's military readiness and its ability to defend its institutions, territory, and people. It further stated that successful operations conducted by the armed forces in recent weeks have delivered an unmistakable message to the Houthi leadership. The era in which cities, civilians, and national infrastructure could be attacked without consequences is over. Any new escalation will bring direct and costly consequences for the military assets, command structures, and capabilities used to carry it out. The Council ordered the military, security, and intelligence services to remain at maximum readiness, reinforce defensive positions, strengthen early-warning systems, and sustain coordinated deterrence operations. It stressed that Houthi forces must be denied the opportunity to gain military or psychological advantage from further escalation. On the economic front, the Council approved continued measures to restore the state's sovereign functions, resources, and control over ports of entry, revenues, and national services. It also ordered stronger action against smuggling networks and channels used to finance terrorism and armed militia activity. The Council stressed that these measures will be implemented in a controlled manner that protects citizens, the private sector, savings, and legitimate financial transfers while safeguarding the flow of food, medicine, fuel, and other essential goods. The Presidential Leadership Council warned that there will be no tolerance for individuals or networks that facilitate smuggling, terrorism financing, or organized crime. It directed the competent authorities to pursue those who organize, enable, protect, or profit from these activities, regardless of their position or status. Anyone proven to have participated in these networks, provided them with assistance, or failed to carry out their legal responsibilities will face accountability. The Council said the objective is to protect Yemen's economy and national resources while cutting the financial lifelines that sustain the Houthi militias and other illicit armed activities. The Council also addressed citizens living in areas held by the Houthi militias, stressing that the state's confrontation is with the armed coup and weapons operating outside legitimate state institutions. It is not a conflict against any region, tribe, community, or religious sect. The Council reaffirmed that the restoration of state authority will be accompanied by the protection of private property, public-sector employment, and citizens' legal rights. It stressed that acts of revenge, lawlessness, exclusion, or marginalization will not be permitted.
